name: District of Columbia
summary: Statutes: the D.C. Code is on code.dccouncil.gov (Council, one page per section, constructible URL, 'Current through Sept. 26, 2026'); the Council's official GitHub repos (law-xml-codified, law-html) give bulk XML/HTML via raw.githubusercontent.com, lagging the site by months; Justia 2025 is the tier-2 fallback. No constitution: the Home Rule Act/District Charter is in D.C. Code Title 1 ch. 2. Court rules and opinions are PDFs on dccourts.gov, whose robots.txt answers with a bot check (script route refused) and which WebFetch read only intermittently; the D.C. App. R. PDF truncates at Rule 41. MOJs are listed by name only. Justia has D.C. Court of Appeals opinions 1923-2026. DCMR text is downloadable .doc files on dcregs.dc.gov (script ok, WebFetch gated); D.C. Register text sits behind postbacks.

citation_map.notes: OUT OF SCOPE, do not route here: the federal U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia ('D.D.C.', CourtListener 'dcd') and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit ('D.C. Cir.', 'cadc'; older 'App. D.C.' / 'U.S. App. D.C.' reporters). The case-law regex only accepts '(D.C. YYYY)' or '(D.C. Mon. D, YYYY)' — '(D.C. Cir. 2020)' and '(D.D.C. 2020)' do not match. Caution: D.C. Circuit decisions before Feb. 1, 1971 are binding D.C. precedent (M.A.P. v. Ryan, 285 A.2d 310 (D.C. 1971)) but are federal reports — route them to federal sources. D.C. has no state constitution: the Home Rule Act (Pub. L. 93-198; D.C. Code §§ 1-201.01 to 1-207.71) serves as the charter; Home Rule Act section numbers (§ 602) map to Code sections (§ 1-206.02) only through the Code's 'Section References'/history notes — no formula. D.C. Code section numbers contain a hyphen (title-section, e.g. 16-1001, 2-1402.11, 29A-1053, 5-545.06a): a range '§§ 16-1001 – 16-1058' is two sections joined by an en dash or 'to'; the regex takes the first. Some sections exist in '(Perm)' and '(Temp)' versions (e.g. 47-2501(Perm)); the suffix is captured but its URL form is untested. 'D.C. Code' with no 'Ann.' is the Bluebook form (Bluebook cites D.C. Code (LexisNexis/West)); practitioners also write 'D.C. Official Code'. Court rules: bare 'Rule 12(b)(6)', 'Civ. R.' or 'Rule 28' must not route here without 'Super. Ct.' / 'D.C. App. R.' / 'D.C. Court of Appeals' context (Delaware also uses 'Super. Ct. Civ. R.' — require D.C. context or a 'D.C.' prefix when the query is ambiguous). The Superior Court Civil Rules track the FRCP numbering, with D.C.-only rules such as 28-I and 12-I. D.C. has no codified rules of evidence (memory; not verified). MOJs (memorandum opinion and judgment) are unpublished; D.C. App. R. 28(g) (fetched 2026-10-16, 2021 revision) says unpublished orders/opinions may not be cited except for law of the case, res judicata, collateral estoppel, same-defendant criminal or same-respondent disciplinary matters. DCCA docket numbers are YY-TT-NNNN (CV civil, CF felony, CM misdemeanor, CO collateral criminal, FS/FM family, AA agency, BG bar); dockets are often cited without leading zeros (22-CO-043 = 22-CO-0843 per Justia listing typo — confirm). The DCCA is the highest local court; review is only by U.S. Supreme Court certiorari. DCMR cites: '14 DCMR § 308' → dcregs SectionNumber '14-308'; subsection '308.1' lives in section 308. CourtListener ids are from memory and unverified; 'dcsuperct' in particular is a guess. FIX 2026-10-17: Superior Court rule cites without a 'D.C.' marker ('Super. Ct. Civ. R. 12(b)(6)', 'Superior Court Civil Rule 60(b)') are shared with Delaware and are now a separate context_required pattern (negative lookbehind for 'Del.'); the distinctive pattern needs 'D.C.' or a D.C.-only division (Dom. Rel., L&T, Sm. Cl., Juv., Neglect, Agency Rev.) or D.C.-only rules 12-I/28-I. 'Court of Appeals Rule N' now requires 'D.C.' (Georgia uses the bare form). The SCOTUS docket pattern is context_required and refuses a 'D.C. Cir.' parenthetical within 40 characters, so federal D.C. Circuit dockets near 'cert.' do not route here. Section numbers accept an en dash (§ 16–1001, as printed on code.dccouncil.gov); normalise it to an ASCII hyphen for URLs.

sources.title: Code of the District of Columbia (D.C. Law Library, code.dccouncil.gov)
sources.publisher: Council of the District of Columbia (Office of the General Counsel), site by Open Law Library
sources.official_status_evidence: Pages carry no official/authentication statement (WebFetch of /code: 'makes no statement about whether this online code is official'); footer says only that codes and laws are public domain. D.C. enacted UELMA (D.C. Law 21-251, D.C. Code §§ 2-651.01 et seq., applying from July 1, 2017) but no designation of this site as official was found.
sources.coverage: Entire D.C. Code (all titles incl. 1 Home Rule, 16, 22, 29A, 47 etc.), with history notes, section references, effect-of-amendments and emergency-legislation notes; one page per section; title pages list chapters with section ranges.

access.pattern_rules: section = the full D.C. Code number exactly as cited, hyphen kept, ASCII hyphen (not the en dash the page heading shows), dots and lower-case letter suffixes kept: 16-1001, 2-1402.11, 1-206.02, 2-651.04, 29A-1053, 5-545.06a. Title index https://code.dccouncil.gov/us/dc/council/code/titles/{title} (titles/16, titles/27A) lists chapters WITH section ranges ('Chapter 10 … §§ 16-1001 – 16-1058'); chapter index /titles/{title}/chapters/{chapter} lists subchapters with ranges. '(Perm)'/'(Temp)' variant URLs untested.

automation.robots_txt: robots.txt (Cloudflare-managed) allows User-Agent * with 'Content-signal: search=yes,ai-train=no' and disallows ClaudeBot, GPTBot, CCBot and other AI crawlers by name, plus '/_*'. fetch_doc.py (its own UA) was allowed. Footer asks: 'Please do not scrape. Instead, bulk download the HTML or XML.' — prefer dc-code-github-xml for anything beyond single lookups.
automation.notes: WebFetch of URLs taken from search results returned full body (2-552, 11-502, /code root); the self-built URL for 16-1001 waited on a permission prompt and timed out (PROVENANCE_REQUIRED) — treat built URLs as gated and use fetch_doc.py. Section pages are short (16-1001 = 4,935 chars; 2-1402.11 = 22,009 chars) so truncation is not a concern.

sources.title: District of Columbia Municipal Regulations (DCMR) — dcregs.dc.gov

access.pattern_rules: 14 DCMR § 308 → SectionNumber=14-308 (metadata only; text is behind a postback 'View Text'). Text route: chapter list https://www.dcregs.dc.gov/Common/DCMR/RuleList.aspx?ChapterNum={title}-{chapter} (chapter = section div 100 for 3-digit sections: 308 → 14-3) — each row's 'View text' anchor carries title/href 'https://dcregs.dc.gov/Common/DCMR/RuleList.aspx?DownloadFile={GUID}' → .doc file (e.g. 14308.doc). GUIDs are not derivable; take from the chapter page. Title list: ChapterList.aspx?TitleNum={title}. TitleList.aspx redirects to ErrorPage.aspx. GUIDs may be braced ({C9DF4839-6F7B-48CC-98F5-D682CF4EAB0B}) and work as-is.
access.navigation: ChapterList.aspx?TitleNum=T → RuleList.aspx?ChapterNum=T-C → `python3 scripts/fetch_doc.py links <RuleList URL> DownloadFile` lists the 'View text' DownloadFile URLs in row order (re-tested 2026-10-17: 17 links for 19 rows on ChapterNum=14-3 — rows without a file are skipped, so order alone can mis-map) → confirm the section with `fetch_doc.py info <url>` (filename=14308.doc = § 308) → grep/verify the .doc text.
